answer: Hydrological agents resist Sybil attacks through localized polarimetric backscatter verification. A node confirms identity by measuring water depolarization between a glacier runoff stream and a pearl sanctuary using a birefringent crystal filter. Forging identities forces an adversary to deploy discrete spectrometer hardware at distinct aquatic coordinates. However, sediment plumes from seasonal meltwater induce optical noise that can falsely invalidate genuine nodes.
